summary.headline: Jindal Steel posted record Q2 FY27 gross revenue of INR 19,448 crore (+44% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR 2,504 crore (+34% YoY) on 2.38 MT sales.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly gross revenue of INR 19,448 crore and record sales volume of 2.38 million tons, with domestic sales about 92% of volume. Adjusted EBITDA rose 34% YoY to INR 2,504 crore, but adjusted EBITDA per ton of INR 10,529 was sequentially lower on higher raw material, power, fuel and freight costs. Net debt fell to INR 14,786 crore and net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 1.51x from 1.71x. Management guided to 11 MT gross steel output in FY27 with H2 net steel of about 6 MT, and said the switch from propane to coal-gas syngas protected productivity during the West Asia supply disruption.

financial_highlights.change: down INR 1,141 crore from INR 15,927 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,228 crore in Q2; INR 3,187 crore in H1

financial_highlights.change: apples-to-apples basis; management says over 65% when excluding low-priced TMT

segments.name: Flat products (HRC and plates)
segments.commentary: Plates production exceeds 220,000 tons per month across both locations; management targets a 65:35 flat-to-long mix, up from about 60:40 currently. Hot-rolled coil output is being shifted to value-added grades such as high and medium carbon.

segments.name: TMT / long products
segments.commentary: TMT output was cut to about 120,000 tons per month from 220,000 tons earlier, with volume redirected to plates and HRC. TMT now goes mainly to major projects.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports run at about 100,000 tons per month, mainly HRC, plates, with some rails and structurals.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Pellet output is about 33,000 tons per day (Barbil 18,000-20,000 and Angul 14,000), all consumed in-house. A new pellet plant is targeted for commercial production by June 2027.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: JSOL (100% subsidiary) turnover and EBITDA are rising as major projects commission; Mozambique coal EBITDA improved YoY on better coal prices.

guidance_outlook: Net steel production target of about 6 MT in H2 FY27 (about 3 MT per quarter, planned at 0.96 MT per month); gross steel about 11 MT for FY27.
Record production expected in Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), with Q4 to exceed Q3.
FY27 sales volume guidance lower end of about 10.5 MT; management says 9-9.5 lakh saleable tons per month is needed and that they are comfortable.
Coking coal cost increase of USD 20-25/ton expected for Q3; a possible further USD 20/ton from diesel and oil if the West Asia conflict prolongs.
Slurry pipeline (192 km, Barbil to Angul) commissioned; commercial supply from about 2-3 days from 23 Oct, saving about INR 700/ton on freight at 20,000 tons per day.
Blast furnace at Angul (about 10,000 tons per day) to ramp to 10,500 in about 7 days, 11,000 in November and 12,000 in December.
Coal gasifier expansion (3 more gasifiers, 35,000 NM3/hr each) and DRI-2 (2 MT) targeted for commissioning by June 2027.
Utkal B2 coal mine clearance expected in FY27; Roida iron ore mine restart expected by about December 2026 to January 2027.
Annual growth capex guided at INR 7,500-10,000 crore; net debt-to-EBITDA to stay below 1.5x through the cycle.
capex_capacity: Blast furnace at Angul ramping to about 10,000 tons per day, targeting 12,000 tons per day by December 2026.
Slurry pipeline: 192 km, commissioned, first iron slurry dispatched, continuous operation planned.
Captive coal mines: about 15 MT total capacity across Raigarh and Angul; captive coal meets about 50-55% of requirement, targeted at 65-70%. Gare Palma about 4 MT.
Kasia iron ore mine at 22,000 tons per day, ramping to 30,000 tons per day.
Coal gasification: 3 additional gasifiers (105,000 NM3/hr combined), over 95% indigenous content, commissioning by June 2027.
Total capex plan of about INR 47,000 crore with INR 8,000-9,000 crore remaining, including DRI-2 and performance-linked payments.
demand_pricing: Average HRC moved from INR 51,000 to INR 60,000/ton during Q2; TMT from INR 52,000 to INR 59,000/ton; structurals INR 60,000-65,000; rails above INR 70,000.
Spot prices around INR 60,000/ton for HRC and TMT as of late October.
Coking coal cost rose about USD 12-15/ton in Q2, within prior guidance; management says prices are stable now.
Propane to coal-gas switch saves about INR 70/kg in reheating furnaces (propane about INR 100/kg vs syngas about INR 30/kg). Management says the company will not revert to propane.
Q2 is seasonally weak for TMT; Q3 expected to be stronger on festive-season construction demand.
Europe steel deficit of about 28 MT cited; EU CBAM and quota remain open issues for exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4.8 MT H1 production run-rate achievable and will flat mix stay at 70:30 in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of about 3 MT per quarter; mix target is 65:35 flat to long, not 70:30, to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much freight saving does the slurry pipeline give, and any extra cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 700/ton on freight with no additional cost; around 500 of 700 daily iron ore trucks to be removed.

qa_highlights.question: Coking coal and West Asia cost impact for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Coking coal up USD 20-25/ton expected in Q3 by Sandeep Modi; West Asia impact on fuel about USD 4-5/ton, steady. Another USD 20/ton possible if conflict prolongs.

qa_highlights.question: Water availability from Brahmani for Angul at higher volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Only 31 MLD being used against 59.1 MLD sanctioned; usage to fall at least 15% next year as Barbil slurry supplies water.

qa_highlights.question: Power sales and their EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said power sales are miniscule relative to the INR 1 lakh crore revenue ambition; no figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Pellet plant and merchant pellet sales?
qa_highlights.answer: No merchant pellet sales now; all 33,000 tons/day consumed in-house. New pellet plant commercial production by June 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and spot price detail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined exact spot prices, citing policy; gave approximate ranges as above.

risks_watch: Coking coal and diesel cost pressure from the West Asia and Russia-Ukraine supply disruptions; management flagged possible USD 20-25/ton in Q3.
Execution on the Angul blast furnace ramp, Roida mine right-of-way, and Utkal B2 approvals.
Possible delays to DRI-2 and coal gasifiers, which management says could slip from June 2027 due to imported equipment.
Other expenses rose about 13% QoQ on freight and power/fuel; management expects normalisation in Q3.
Water availability at Angul given the Brahmani river reservoir level, though management says consumption will be lower.
EU quota and CBAM outcomes that determine export access.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on production ramp-up, cost savings and balance sheet, with management repeatedly describing the company as cash surplus. Evasive on exact ASP, spot prices, power sales and subsidiary-level numbers, which it declined to quantify on the call.
key_quotes: So, we are quite confident that we'll be in a position to achieve these 3 million tons per quarter.
And INR 700 per ton will be saving on freight and no additional expenses.
So, we don't want to invest money unless we reach to our 100% capacity utilization.
So, the steel scenario is very good. I think it is now around 10% Y-o-Y basis, there's a growth.

adds.what: 192 km Barbil-Angul slurry pipeline (commissioned, commercial supply from 23 Oct)
3 additional coal gasifiers (35,000 NM3/hr each, 105,000 NM3/hr combined)
New pellet plant, commercial production targeted June 2027
Angul blast furnace ramp from ~10,000 tpd to 12,000 tpd by Dec 2026 (debottlenecking of existing unit)

growth.why: Management reaffirmed ~11 MT FY27 gross steel output and 9-9.5 lakh saleable tons/month, backed by Angul blast furnace ramp to 12,000 tpd by December, slurry pipeline and coal mine/gasifier/DRI additions due around June 2027, though FY27 volume guided only to the lower end of ~10.5 MT and no order book cited.
